pages.title: Executive summary
pages.intro: Nika is a multi-brand operating workspace and CRM for Applitent and Ofogh Nikan. It combines client operations, delivery control, evidence, communication, staff workflows, finance, integrations, auditability, and operational intelligence in one Laravel application. The repository is feature-rich but explicitly remains an implementation-in-progress system rather than a deployment candidate.

pages.title: What Nika is - and what it is not

blocks.text: Operational system, not a contact list

Nika treats CRM as an operating layer around clients and work. Client records connect to inquiries, opportunities, cases, tasks, commitments, documents, approvals, appointments, calls, finance records, communication, attendance-related availability, notifications, and audit events.

items: The existing Applitent portal remains authoritative for pre-cutover records; Nika is designed to ingest new post-cutover submissions.
WhatsApp and Telegram stay manual; no paid AI or n8n dependency is part of the current operating model.
Payroll rules are not fabricated. Iran payroll remains deferred until validated business and legal rules are supplied.
Deployment, rollback packaging, full browser acceptance, and several live external adapters remain future readiness work.

cards.title: Laravel application
cards.text: Laravel 13 on PHP 8.3+ with server-rendered application flows, controllers, services, policies through service checks, and relational persistence.

cards.title: Database-backed runtime
cards.text: Database sessions and queues are first-class. Stateful workflows rely on durable records, version fields, audit events, and idempotency keys.

cards.title: Frontend delivery
cards.text: Blade/Vite assets are local rather than CDN-dependent. The UI supports light, dark, and system themes plus Persian RTL rendering.

cards.title: Authentication
cards.text: Laravel Fortify provides account authentication, password reset, password confirmation, and optional TOTP multi-factor authentication.

cards.title: Queue + scheduler
cards.text: Background mail, integration processing, reminders, heartbeats, and recovery checks use database queues and the Laravel scheduler.

cards.title: Language + locale
cards.text: English, Persian, and Spanish are configured, with Asia/Tehran as the default user timezone and explicit timezone-aware appointment handling.

blocks.text: Client visibility follows real operational relationships

The CEO can see all clients. Other users see clients they created or clients connected to work that falls inside their current visibility scope. This keeps client access aligned with operational responsibility instead of exposing the whole database.

Signed post-cutover integration submissions are normalized into CRM intake records and source mappings. New external submissions enter the manager queue without an owner so assignment remains a deliberate operational action.

The current design does not attempt to seize ownership of all historical Applitent portal data. Existing records remain with the established portal; the integration boundary is for new submissions after connector cutover and for controlled source updates that do not overwrite CRM-owned fields.
